codex.note: Codex has no auto-compact window or subagent model default to set; the instruction line carries the rules.

instructions.claude: - Usage: follow the `lean-usage` skill. Set an explicit `model` on every subagent by task, and a cheaper one only with no obvious loss of quality (Fable 5.2 at low or medium effort, never high, for 3D, VFX, UI and visual work and small tested code; Opus 5.5 for big or hard coding, and Opus 5.5 at high effort for coordinators; Sonnet 5.5 for reading many files and retrieval; Haiku with care, only for read-only jobs such as searches or gathering memory context, never for edits or decisions). Do small jobs inline. At most 2 subagents at once, no forks. Use contact sheets, not piles of screenshots. Time-limit every wait or background command. Put read-only steps that follow each other in one Bash call, and run only the checks for what you changed until the final full run. Compact at breakpoints, and start a fresh session with a handoff memory when the task changes.
instructions.codex: - Usage: follow the `lean-usage` skill in `~/.codex/skills/lean-usage/`. Read its Claude terms as Codex equivalents: subagents are parallel tasks or agents, Opus/Sonnet/Haiku are your strongest/standard/fastest models, and `/compact` is starting a fresh session with a handoff note. Do small jobs inline. At most 2 parallel agents. Time-limit every wait. Keep context small.
